commits.pr_title: [Feature][Humming] Humming feature integration
commits.pr_body:
This PR expands Humming quantization support and integrates a unified input processing kernel.

#### 1. Hadamard transforms for online quantization

Enable Hadamard transforms by setting `hadamard_block_size` in `VLLM_HUMMING_ONLINE_QUANT_CONFIG`.

#### 2. SM120/SM121 support

Add support for NVFP4, MXFP4, and MXFP8, including the non-public `float4e0m3` and `float8e3m4` data types, see https://github.com/vllm-project/humming/pull/41 .

#### 3. Additional input quantization modes

Support `static_per_tensor`, `static_tensor_dynamic_group`, and `dynamic_group_tensor`. The latter two primarily serve NVFP4 quantization.

#### 4. Checkpoint quantization and input schema fallback

Honor checkpoint input quantization settings and automatically fall back to a higher-precision input schema when the device does not support the configured activation quantization type.

To retain the original WNA16 behavior, set:

```bash
export VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"bfloat16"}'
```

Input schemas explicitly specified through `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` disable fallback by default. Unsupported configurations raise an error unless `"allow_fallback": true` is explicitly specified.

#### 5. Unified `process_input` kernel

Support fused combinations of optional activation function, Hadamard transforms, and input quantization across multiple layouts.

Custom activations support `unary`, `binary_split`, and `binary_interleaved` modes, with implementations supplied as CUDA C++ expressions.

| Path | Gemm Type | Fused operations | Padding handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dense | `dense` | Optional Hadamard transform and input quantization | — |
| MoE gate/up | `indexed` | Optional Hadamard transform and input quantization | — |
| MoE gate/up | `grouped_contiguous` | MoE permutation, optional Hadamard transform and input quantization | Skip invalid padding tokens in EP |
| MoE gate/up | `grouped_mask` | Optional Hadamard transform and input quantization | Skip invalid padding tokens |
| MoE down | `indexed` | Activation, optional Hadamard transform and input quantization | Skip invalid padding tokens in EP |
| MoE down | `grouped_contiguous` | Activation, optional Hadamard transform and input quantization | Skip invalid padding tokens in EP |
| MoE down | `grouped_mask` | Activation, optional Hadamard transform and input quantization | Skip invalid padding tokens |

#### 6. Additional scatter indices

Extend `moe_permute` and `moe_align_block_size` to return the `scatter_idx` required by `process_input`.

#### 7. Humming mxfp6 backend

Add `HummingMxFp6LinearKernel`.

#### 8. Humming utility refactoring

Refactor `humming_utils.py`, moving some validation and conversion logic into the Humming library.

#### 9. Type annotations

Add type annotations to `vllm/utils/humming.py`.

commits.pr_title: [DSV4.1] Add encoder cuda graph support for deepseek-v4.1-flash
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Enable CUDA graph capture/replay for the DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder (ViT +
aligner) via the `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` protocol, removing per-image eager
encoder overhead (Python loop, per-image kernel launches, RoPE/cu_seqlens
host computation) from the request critical path.

The captured graph packs a batch of images into one varlen run: ViT blocks
attend per image via `cu_seqlens`, and the aligner's spatial merge becomes a
gather+mask against precomputed indices. Enabled with
`--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'`.

## Test Plan

### Setup

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (real weights, FP8 + FP4 experts)
- Hardware: 1 node, 4 x NVIDIA GB200 (SM100), TP=4
- Attention backend: `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` (the SM100-default
  `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` is currently broken upstream for this checkpoint:
  `finalize_mega_attn_weights` permutes `wq_b` assuming the pre-repack
  `[out, in]` layout, but the MXFP8 quant finalize has already transposed it
  to MN-major -- unrelated to this change)
- Server: `vllm serve ... --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64`
- A/B: identical server + client, only `cudagraph_mm_encoder` toggled.
  With the flag on, 9 budget graphs were captured (64..16384 tokens),
  ViT attention backend `FLASH_ATTN`.

### Commands

```bash
# Server (encoder CG off / on)
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 \
    [--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}']

# Benchmark: VisionArena-Chat, 256 requests, concurrency 32, 32 output tokens
vllm bench serve \
    --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
    --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --dataset-name hf --dataset-path lmarena-ai/VisionArena-Chat \
    --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32 \
    --output-len 32 --ignore-eos \
    --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el

# e2e unit test
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -k deepseek_v41
```

## Test Result

### Benchmark (VisionArena-Chat, 256 reqs, avg ~446 input tokens incl. image)

| Metric                 | Encoder CG off | Encoder CG on | Speedup |
|------------------------|----------------|---------------|---------|
| Benchmark duration (s) | 64.08          | 24.68         | 2.60x   |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 4.00       | 10.37         | 2.60x   |
| Mean TTFT (ms)         | 4467           | 1894          | 2.36x   |
| Median TTFT (ms)       | 4441           | 691           | 6.43x   |
| P99 TTFT (ms)          | 21348          | 4570          | 4.67x   |
| Mean TPOT (ms)         | 114.2          | 38.3          | 2.98x   |
| Mean E2E latency (ms)  | 8007           | 3081          | 2.60x   |
| P99 E2E latency (ms)   | 21620          | 4858          | 4.45x   |

TPOT also improves because eager per-image encoder runs no longer interleave
with (and preempt) decode iterations.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Expose per-request spec decode metrics in generate API
commits.pr_body:
### Summary

Expose the existing opt-in per-request speculative decoding metrics in the token-in/token-out `/inference/v1/generate` API through the same `metrics.speculative_decoding` response shape used by the OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Full responses include metrics for single-sequence requests. Streaming follows Chat/Completion: metrics are returned once in the final usage chunk (`choices=[]`) when `stream_options.include_usage=true`; token chunks are unchanged. Chat and Completion derendering preserve the metrics object. Python suppresses request-level metrics for `n>1`; Rust rejects parallel sampling.

Requires `--per-request-spec-decode-metrics`; collection remains disabled by default. Python and Rust frontends are covered. This does not change model execution or sampling.

### Why this is not duplicate work

#48915 provides the shared metrics pipeline and OpenAI API exposure. This PR exposes that same pipeline through the separate token-in/token-out API without another scheduler accumulator or a second public schema.

### Validation

- Python spec-metrics tests: 6 passed, covering full/stream responses, terminal usage placement, and `n>1` suppression.
- Streaming derender metrics passthrough test passed.
- Rust `vllm-server` generate tests: 62 passed, including streaming and non-streaming metrics propagation and JSON serialization.
- Changed-file pre-commit passed, including mypy, ruff, markdownlint, and Rust format.
- GB200 E2E: Qwen3-0.6B with n-gram speculation returned identical metrics in the full response and final streaming usage chunk; token chunks contained no metrics.

### AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation and tests. Claude performed multiple read-only adversarial review rounds. Human review remains required.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Skip non-prefix-cacheable groups in SimpleCPUOffload (GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail and QSA)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash carries a kpool-tail scratch group (`KpoolTailSpec`, `prefix_cacheable=False`, `block_size=index_kpool=4`) next to prefix-cacheable groups that hash at 1152 tokens on this box (MLA 1152, 4× Mamba 1152 in `align` mode). Core (`resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`, `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`, `KVCacheManager`) and the `MooncakeStore connector` already skip such groups. `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` did not, and treated every KV cache group as offloadable:

- `_select_eager_blocks_to_store` views the request hashes at each group's block size to build `BlockStored` metadata. For the tail group that is `resolve_block_hashes(hashes, hash_block_size=1152, block_size=4)`, which trips the divisibility assert as soon as `--kv-events-config` enables KV cache events. The engine dies on the first prefill store.
- `update_state_after_alloc` maps external (CPU-hit) tokens onto the scratch group and asserts alignment against its block size, although the coordinator never returns hit blocks for it.

This PR records which groups take part in offloading (`prefix_cacheable`) and skips the rest in eager store selection and in load pairing. Scratch blocks never carry a hash, so nothing is stored or loaded for them either way; the scratch slot in the per-group hit tuple stays empty, exactly as the coordinator leaves it.


## Duplication check

Two open PRs touch the same code path: #55033 (draft since 2026-09-02, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA ring, also adjusts `_estimate_lazy_target_blocks`) and #56404 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, gates `resolve_block_hashes` in the store path only, currently conflicting). This PR is scoped to the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool-tail layout and adds what neither of them covers: a regression test for the actual crash trigger (`enable_kv_cache_events=true`, `BlockStored` emitted for cacheable groups only) and an end-to-end store/load + accuracy check on GLM-5.3-Flash. Happy to fold the test into #55033 instead if the maintainers prefer to land that one. #54743 applies the same scoping to the *OffloadingConnector* (`build_offloading_config`) and does not touch `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload`; the two are complementary.

## Test Plan

Unit:

```
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
    tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py -q
```

E2E: GLM-5.3-Flash, 4× GB300, TP4 + EP, `--enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 32768`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` with 16 GB pinned host memory per rank, `--kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq"}'`, dev endpoint `/reset_prefix_cache` used to evict the GPU prefix cache between runs (`?reset_external=true` also clears the CPU pool).

## Test Result

E2E store/load (10,277-token prompt, greedy, 32 new tokens):

| step | GPU prefix hit | connector hit |
|---|---|---|
| fresh | 0 / 10277 | 0 / 10277 |
| same prompt again | 9216 / 10277 | 0 / 1061 |
| after `/reset_prefix_cache` | 0 / 10277 | 9216 / 10277 |
| after `/reset_prefix_cache` again | 0 / 10277 | 9216 / 10277 |

Hits are 1152-aligned (the Mamba/MLA block); the kpool tail block is a fresh per-request scratch block at every resume, as with a GPU hit.

Accuracy (4 natural-text prompts built from `docs/`, 3.4k–24k tokens, `max_tokens=16`, greedy, `logprobs=20` at the first generated position; every case compared against the first fresh run of the same prompt):

| case | top-1 \|Δlogprob\| mean / max | mean \|Δlogprob\| over shared top-20 | max \|Δlogprob\| | identical 16-token greedy output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fresh again (no cache at all) | 0.10 / 0.25 | 0.42 | 2.06 | 3 / 4 |
| GPU prefix hit | 0.13 / 0.31 | 0.27 | 1.03 | 2 / 4 |
| CPU (connector) hit | 0.11 / 0.16 | 0.28 | 0.91 | 3 / 4 |
| CPU hit, second time | 0.11 / 0.12 | 0.32 | 1.88 | 3 / 4 |

The CPU-hit deltas sit inside the band that two *fresh* recomputations of the same prompt already show on this model/backend (the fresh-vs-fresh spread is not caused by this PR; it is present with the connector disabled as well, see the `fresh again` row), so the offload round trip adds no measurable error over a plain GPU prefix hit.

AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude Code (analysis, patch, tests and the reproduction scripts); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][GLM] Fuse the kpool tail slot mapping into one Triton kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash sparse-MLA models keep a one-block-per-request circular tail cache (kpool). Every decode step — twice per step with MTP, once for the target model and once for the drafter — `KpoolTailMetadataBuilder.build()` maps each token to its request's tail ring with a chain of small torch ops (`arange` + `searchsorted` + `clamp` + `index_select` + `remainder` + `copy_`): 12 kernel launches and ~250 us of CPU enqueue time per build.

This PR replaces the chain with a single Triton kernel driven directly by `query_start_loc`, including the CUDA-graph padding rows. The CPU-tensor path keeps the torch implementation, and the emitted values are bit-identical to it.

With #57317 the generic `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` no longer runs for `KpoolTailSpec`, so `compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping` is now the only slot-mapping path for the tail group — this fusion covers all of it. It composes with #57477 (the seed-kernel stride fix): this PR only produces the logical slot ids (`block * kpool + pos % kpool`) that consumers decompose with `// kpool` / `% kpool`; physical addressing of the padded tail view is untouched, and the kernel reads the block table through its real `stride(0)`.

Not a duplicate: #56562 covers the sparse-indexer decode expansion and the token→request mapping (an earlier revision of this PR had similar pieces and was rescoped); #57161 reworks the kpool *compress* kernel and #57458 the NoPE query packing — neither touches the tail slot mapping.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py
```

E2E setup: 4x GB300 (SM103), TP4, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE), `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE --max-model-len 69632 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, V2 model runner; `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos`, two runs per build, base = `42a33039eb`.

## Test Result

- `test_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py`: 17 passed — 4 new CUDA cases check the Triton path against the torch reference, including tokens past the last request boundary, CUDA-graph padding rows, and a non-contiguous (strided-view) block table.
- `test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py` + `test_indexer_native_next_n.py`: 16 passed.
- Bit-exact vs the torch formulation → no output-affecting change, so no separate model eval was run.

Micro (`compute_kpool_tail_slot_mapping`, kpool=4, GB300; CPU = enqueue time without sync, GPU = profiler device time):

E2E (8k in / 1k out, output tok/s, two runs per build):

| point | main | +this PR | Δ (avg) | main run-to-run noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | 220.1 / 215.3 | 229.0 / 228.7 | +5.1% | ±2.2% |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3-Flash] Address kpool tail blocks by the padded indexer stride in the NVIDIA prefill seed kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix silent indexer-cache corruption for GLM-5.3-Flash on NVIDIA: the kpool prefill tail-seed kernel addresses tail blocks with a dense stride while the tail cache is stored with the indexer's padded block stride.

**How the tail cache is laid out.** `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` pads the `KpoolTailSpec` page to the indexer page (`page_size_padded = idx_page`; 38016 B for the default `block_size=1152`: 288 pool rows x 132 B), and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` places every indexer layer's tail tensor at the *same offset* as that layer's indexer tensor with `block_stride = idx_page`. Tail block `b` is therefore the first 2048 B (`[2, kpool=4, 128]` bf16) of indexer block `b`; the two never collide because both groups draw distinct block ids from one pool. `create_kv_cache_views` builds the view with `as_strided`, so `tail_kv_cache.stride(0) == 19008` elements instead of the dense 1024.

**The bug.** `_kpool_tail_seed_kernel` in `vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/kpool_compress.py` computed

```python
base = (blk * 2 * KPOOL + t % KPOOL) * HEAD_DIM   # dense 2048 B block stride
```

so for every prefill it (a) left the request's own tail block unseeded and (b) wrote 2048 B of raw bf16 K / gate rows at byte `blk * 2048` of the layer's indexer region, i.e. into indexer block `blk * 2048 // 38016` at offset `blk * 2048 % 38016` — fp8 key rows or the fp32 scale region of whatever request owns that block. The decode kernel (`TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS` / `KPOOL_HEAD`) and the AMD seed kernel already address the tail through `stride(0)` / `stride(1)`; only the NVIDIA seed kernel did not, and the existing regression test for exactly this layout was `skipif(not is_rocm)`.

**Why it shows up as "the cached system prompt is broken".** Only indexer blocks with id below `num_blocks * 2048 / 38016` (~5% of the pool) can be hit, and those are the ids handed out first after startup, i.e. the blocks of the first prefix-cached prompt, typically a long-lived system prompt. Every later request whose tail block id falls in `[19, ~19 * k]` overwrites part of that prompt's indexer blocks `1..k`; prefix-cached blocks are never recomputed, so the damage persists and accumulates, on every TP rank identically. The MLA KV itself is untouched (all writes stay inside the layer's indexer region), so the effect is a corrupted sparse top-k selection for any context longer than `index_topk` (2048). The predicted signature is therefore: with prefix caching on, requests that hit a long-lived cached prompt degrade over time while the same prompt sent with a `cache_salt` (fresh, high block ids) stays correct even on repeated cache hits, and all TP ranks are affected identically. The reproduction below confirms exactly this.

**Fix.** Pass `TAIL_BLOCK_ELEMS = tail.stride(0)` and `KPOOL_HEAD = tail.stride(1)` to the NVIDIA seed kernel (same as the AMD kernel), assert the expected view layout in `kpool_seed_tail_cache`, and run `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` on every platform.

**Origin.** The tail cache has aliased the indexer tensor with a padded, strided view since the tail spec was introduced on the GLM-5.3-Flash development branch (07-28); the prefill seed was a torch fancy-index scatter (`tail[block_ids, 0, offsets] = k`, stride-correct) until it was replaced by this Triton kernel with dense addressing (08-17, "perf: indexer eager path tail seed and scatter"). The kernel reached main unchanged with #53906 and is unchanged in the current main, so every NVIDIA build since #53906 is affected.

**Not a duplicate.** #56059 adds a `NUM_TAIL_BLOCKS` out-of-range guard to the same kernel for a ROCm fault (#56037); it does not change the addressing, and the two changes compose. No other open PR touches the NVIDIA seed kernel's addressing.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py -q
```

Kernel-level repro (SM103): build the runtime tail view with `create_kv_cache_views(KpoolTailSpec(block_size=4, num_kv_heads=2, head_size=128, dtype=bf16, page_size_padded=38016), ...)` over a sentinel-filled 256 x 38016 B buffer, seed one 6-token request whose tail block is 200 (and 18), then inspect which bytes changed.

End-to-end byte-level probe (GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 on 4 x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, prefix caching on, `num_gpu_blocks_override=800` so the block pool wraps every ~130 requests): an offline `LLM` serves a 14.5k-token system prompt of 420 "vault -> access code" records, then `collective_rpc` snapshots the indexer K cache pages and the tail cache of the prompt's blocks on rank 0. Eight rounds of 50 unrelated filler prompts (200-2000 tokens each) follow; after every round one lookup question re-hits the cached prompt (keeping it hot in the LRU) and the cached pages are diffed against the snapshot taken right after the first request. Finally seven lookup questions are asked against the hot cached prompt. Same script, same seed, on main and on this branch.

Server: main, TP4, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `enforce_eager`, `--num-gpu-blocks-override 800` so the block pool cycles quickly (with the default pool the same script needs several thousand fillers).

## Test Result

Kernel-level repro, tail view `stride = (19008, 512, 128, 1)` elements:

| kernel | tail block | own tail block seeded | bytes written (layer indexer region) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 200 | no (still sentinel) | `[409600, 411648)` = indexer block 10, fp8 rows 230..245 |
| main | 18 | no | `[36864, 38912)` = indexer block 0 scale region + block 1 rows 0..6 |
| this PR | 200 | yes | `[7603200, 7605248)` = block 200, bytes 0..2048 |
| this PR | 18 | yes | `[684288, 686336)` = block 18, bytes 0..2048 |

`pytest tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py`: on main the un-skipped `test_prefill_seed_honors_padded_tail_block_stride` fails (`tail[3, 0, 2]` is still the sentinel); with this PR 29 passed, 1 skipped (ROCm-only preshuffle test).

End-to-end probe. Runtime views match the analysis: indexer `k_cache` `[7200, 32, 132]` uint8 stride `(4224, 132, 1)` (800 blocks x 9 DeepGEMM pages) and `tail_cache` `[800, 2, 4, 128]` bf16 stride `(19008, 512, 128, 1)` share one `data_ptr`. The system prompt occupies indexer blocks 1..13; the 38 fully cached pages of blocks 1..5 were watched.

| filler requests since the prompt was cached | main: cached pages modified | main: bytes modified | main: re-hit lookup | this PR: pages modified | this PR: re-hit lookup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 16 / 38 | 18.4 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 100 | 21 / 38 | 28.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 150 | 21 / 38 | 36.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 200 | 24 / 38 | 41.6 KB | correct | 0 | correct |
| 250 | 25 / 38 | 45.7 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 300 | 25 / 38 | 47.8 KB | no code | 0 | correct |
| 350 | 27 / 38 | 58.0 KB | wrong code | 0 | correct |
| 400 | 30 / 38 | 64.1 KB | no code | 0 | correct |

Final seven lookups against the hot cached prompt: main 1/7 correct, with garbled answers such as `vault harbor-harbor-7` and `raven-saffron-203? No, wait`; this PR 7/7 correct. The modified regions on main are contiguous 2048 B runs (e.g. page 9 offsets 0..2816), i.e. one misplaced tail seed per filler request, and on main the very first request already writes 2048 B into indexer block 0 (the null block); neither happens with this PR. commits.pr_title: [Core][Kernel] Share persistent workspaces for Marlin and Humming
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Co-authored by: ErinYin <liang.yin@daocloud.io>

Humming grouped MoE currently retains permutation scratch in every layer, so its persistent memory grows with the number of layers. Marlin lock buffers are also owned by individual layers or kernels, tying their lifetime to weight preparation and reload.

This PR gives both resources a shared owner in `WorkspaceManager`:

- Add `get_persistent_resource(key, factory)` for objects with stable storage and `get_persistent(...)` for fixed-shape tensors. Resources are cached separately for each `(ubatch, lane)` and must exist before workspace locking.
- Share compatible Humming `MoEPermuteScratch` objects across sequential layers. Compatibility includes capacity, routing dimensions, device, hidden size, and dtype.
- Acquire Marlin locks at execution time, with separate buffers for concurrent CUDA streams as well as ubatches and lanes. Zero-initialize once; successful Marlin calls restore their counters to zero.
- Resolve dense Marlin workspace lookup inside a runtime custom op so `torch.compile` does not trace execution-context selection.
- Preserve standalone allocation when no workspace manager exists and support explicit Marlin workspaces.

### Relationship to existing work

This combines the direction of #50626 and #56764 with a general resource API. #50626 is the earlier tensor-only Marlin implementation; #56764 adds a Humming-specific cache and accessor to `WorkspaceManager`. Here, the manager handles resource lifetime and execution-slot isolation, while each backend defines its own resource and compatibility key. The intent is to consolidate both changes around that shared API.

Addresses the memory issue in #56759 and relates to the runtime-storage ownership discussion in #48312. Searches for those issues and for `marlin workspace`, `workspace persistent`, and `humming scratch` found the related PRs above; the distinction is the combined, backend-independent resource API.

#55105 remains complementary: its dispatch-capacity and runtime-dtype fixes can feed into the shared scratch accessor, while its activation-buffer fixes stay in Humming. Those fixes are not included here.

## Test Plan

Tests cover resource reuse and locking, standalone fallback, isolation across execution slots and CUDA streams, weight-preparation behavior, and compiled Marlin execution. Permutation tests compare outputs with and without persistent scratch; CUDA graph tests change inputs, routing, and graph sizes to detect stale metadata or aliasing.

Latest targeted runs on NVIDIA B300:

```bash
# 488 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  -k 'permute or humming or workspace or persistent' --timeout=180 -q

# 20 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_isolated_across_execution_slots \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed; run with FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via PYTHONPATH
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_reused_across_graph_sizes \
  --timeout=180 -q

# 112 passed, 13 skipped
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_tile_padding.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  -k 'marlin or workspace' --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py -k persistent_locks -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run
git diff --check
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, and repository checks.

Before publication, the commit was rebased onto `f3aa88d230`. The only conflict was an obsolete Marlin workspace docstring; the implementation was preserved. Hooks passed again, followed by **60 passed** in this focused run (FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via `PYTHONPATH`):

```bash
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py \
  -k 'persistent or humming or scratch or marlin_prepare_layer or marlin_post_load or marlin_workspace' \
  --timeout=180 -q
```

## Test Result

### Humming memory

Before the rebase, compared clean base `35dc273072ff133743bc5fcfa306bf030fa8730b` with this change using the same compiled extensions and dependency versions. Model: `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`, revision `a1ff8c8967426709e5528307c14c52c17616b008` (40 MoE layers, hidden size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8).

Configuration: one B300, TP=1/DP=1, BF16, Humming for linear and MoE, **`VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped`**. Worker probes confirmed all 40 layers used `HummingGroupedExperts`. Fixed 8 GiB KV cache, max model length 8192, max sequences 32, async scheduling disabled, seed 0, V2 runner, compilation and CUDA graphs enabled with capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.17.

Live PyTorch GPU allocation immediately after initialization, in GiB (2^30 bytes):

| Max batched tokens | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2048 | 33.412 | 30.953 | **2.459** |
| 8192 | 41.352 | 31.516 | **9.836** |

The number of scratch objects falls from 40 to 1. At 8192 tokens, their storage falls from 10330.684 MiB to 258.267 MiB: **97.5% less scratch memory**. Each distinct configuration or concurrently active execution slot still needs separate storage. Fixing the KV-cache budget keeps vLLM from consuming the saving as a larger KV cache.

The 8192-token pair ran sequentially on the same reserved GPU, with fresh processes. The 2048-token baseline and repeated full baseline used another B300 of the same model. These measurements do not establish a latency improvement.

### Model evaluation

Full GSM8K with the grouped Humming configuration above, 1319 questions, five shots, greedy sampling, and a 256-output-token limit, using the repository's GSM8K prompt/scoring helpers:

| Run | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1208/1319 | 91.58% | 1 |
| After | 1203/1319 | 91.21% | 1 |
| Before, repeated control | 1201/1319 | 91.05% | 1 |

The candidate falls within the observed baseline accuracy range. This does **not** establish bitwise equivalence or rule out a causal accuracy effect: 690/1319 token sequences match between before/after, while only 669/1319 match between the two unmodified baseline runs. Repeated greedy requests also vary on both versions, including after prefix-cache resets; the cause remains unresolved.

Marlin additionally passed the repository GSM8K serving evaluation on 128 questions with five shots: **119/128 (92.97%), zero invalid answers**, using the same model with both backends set to Marlin, max sequences 16, max batched tokens 2048, and graph sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`.

### Remaining validation

No H200 or end-to-end distributed DeepEP v2/HT/LL, DBO, or DSpark serving run was performed. Expert-map and execution-slot tests cover local behavior and do not substitute for those runs. The model evaluation uses BF16/SILU and does not cover the FP8/SITU cases discussed in #55105.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting this PR.

## Summary

Replace the ROCm DeepSeek V4 BF16 `wo_a` output-projection path on gfx950 with:

1. AITER `inverse_rope_group_quant`, which fuses inverse RoPE with per-token
   E8M0 group quantization.
2. AITER `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale`, which consumes the quantized activation
   and the checkpoint's native FP8 `wo_a` weight.

This removes the BF16 grouped einsum and keeps `wo_a` in its checkpoint FP8
form. Unsupported weights, scales, devices, and older AITER installations
retain the existing BF16 fallback.

## Dependency

This fast path requires AITER >= 0.1.20, which added the MX-scale batched GEMM.
It therefore depends on #52826. Current `main` remains safe: the capability
probe logs once and falls back to BF16 when the op is unavailable.

## Implementation

- Reuse the existing `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM` gate and restrict the path to
  gfx950.
- Accept native `float8_e8m0fnu`/`uint8` scales, or losslessly convert positive
  power-of-two FP32 scales to biased E8M0 exponent bytes.
- Validate the group-128 weight and scale layouts before enabling the path.
- Cache contiguous BF16 cosine/sine cache views once after weight loading.
- Preserve the existing `rocm_inv_rope_einsum` path as the fallback.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Bound the prompt after multimodal expansion
commits.pr_body:
FIX https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57038

## Purpose

`truncate_prompt_tokens` is applied before multimodal placeholder expansion, so the rendered prompt can exceed the requested limit. With Qwen3-ASR, asking for 96 tokens returns 147: truncation keeps 96 unexpanded tokens, then one audio placeholder expands into 52, giving `96 - 1 + 52`.

The two steps run in this order, and nothing re-checks the bound between them:

```python
# vllm/renderers/base.py::BaseRenderer.render_cmpl
dict_prompts = self.render_prompts(prompts)
tok_prompts = self.tokenize_prompts(dict_prompts, tok_params)   # truncates here
...
return [
    self.process_for_engine(prompt, arrival_time, ...)          # expands here
    for prompt in tok_prompts
]
```

`tokenize_prompts` ends in `TokenizeParams.apply_post_tokenization`, which truncates the still-unexpanded token ids:

```python
# vllm/renderers/params.py::TokenizeParams._validate_tokens
for validator in (
    self._token_truncation,
    self._token_padding,
    self._token_len_check,
):
    tokens = validator(tokenizer, tokens)
```

`process_for_engine` then reaches `_process_multimodal`, which expands the placeholders. It never received `tok_params`, so the requested limit was not available at that point.

This adds `BaseRenderer._truncate_expanded_prompt`, which re-applies the bound once placeholders are expanded, and threads `tok_params` through `process_for_engine` / `_process_singleton` as an optional keyword argument. The one external caller, `entrypoints/pooling/scoring/io_processor.py`, is unaffected, and encoder-decoder prompts keep their current behaviour.

Multimodal spans are never cut. A request whose spans would not all survive the truncation is rejected with `VLLMValidationError`, matching the existing post-expansion rejection in `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py::_validate_model_input`. Cutting mid-span would leave the audio features and placeholder metadata disagreeing with the token ids, and silently dropping an item would change the meaning of the request. Happy to switch to dropping or to rejecting outright if you prefer.

No open PR addresses this issue; it had no linked PRs and no comments when I started.

## Test Plan

New unit coverage in `tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py`: the reported case, an under-limit no-op, a split span, a span dropped entirely past the cut, left-side truncation shifting placeholder offsets, and no limit requested. These call `_truncate_expanded_prompt` directly, so they need no model weights and no GPU.

```bash
pytest tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py -v
pytest tests/renderers/ -q
ruff check vllm/renderers/base.py tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py
ruff format --check vllm/renderers/base.py tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py
python repro_57038.py   # reproducer from the issue
```

## Test Result

```text
pytest tests/renderers/test_truncate_after_mm_expansion.py -v
6 passed

pytest tests/renderers/ -q
4 failed, 498 passed, 2 skipped

ruff check / ruff format --check
All checks passed! / 2 files already formatted
```

The 4 failures are pre-existing and unrelated: they fail identically with this change reverted (`test_cohere.py::test_async_cohere_renderer_does_not_block_event_loop`, two `test_hf.py::test_resolve_content_format_hf_defined` parametrisations, and `test_multimodal_hashes.py::test_mm_hash_includes_uuid_and_processing_kwargs`). One surfaces a `PixtralRotaryEmbedding` import error from the installed transformers version.

The reproducer from the issue, before and after:

```text
before: Requested token limit: 96 | Returned tokens: 147 | Matches full prompt[:96]: False
after:  Requested token limit: 96 | Returned tokens:  96 | Matches full prompt[:96]: True
```

Verified on `main` at dffbb714e, torch 2.13.0+cu129.

No model evaluation: this path validates and truncates request prompts before they reach the engine, and does not change model execution, kernels, or sampling. Prompts that already fit the requested limit are byte-identical to before.

AI assistance was used to reproduce the issue and analyse the call path. I have read and tested every line of this change.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Pass intermediate_tensors to the model when capturing CUDA gr…
commits.pr_body:
The V2 execution path always puts "intermediate_tensors" into model_inputs (gpu/model_runner.py), but the capture path only adds it on non-first pipeline ranks. With PP=1 the key is therefore never present, and the capture calls model(**model_inputs) without it.

Models that declare intermediate_tensors as a required positional argument fail there with a TypeError during engine start-up, while the very same model runs fine once serving starts. Every top-level model currently in the registry defaults the argument to None, so nothing is broken today, but the capture and execution paths disagree and the next model that omits the default will hit this again.

Insert the key before **prepare_dummy_inputs() so the non-first-rank branch can still override it, matching gpu/model_runner.py and the V1 runner.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][EPD] Support dynamic EPD (EC-connector) proxy
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add launcher-managed dynamic instance registration to the existing EPD example
proxy while preserving its static URL configuration mode.

An external launcher can register ready instances over HTTP as `encode`,
`prefill`, `decode`, or `prefill_decode`. The registered roles determine the
topology:

- `encode` + `prefill_decode` for E+PD
- `encode` + `prefill` + `decode` for E+P+D

The proxy rejects mixing combined PD instances with standalone P/D instances.
A standalone decode instance is routable only while a healthy prefill instance
is available.

This change is confined to the example proxy, its launch scripts, documentation,
and tests. It does not add worker registration threads or change vLLM's EC
connector configuration.

## Usage

Start the proxy in dynamic mode with an admin key:

```bash
export ADMIN_API_KEY="your-admin-key"
python examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py \
  --port 8000 --dynamic-registration
```

After an instance is ready, register its reachable HTTP endpoint:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body http://proxy-host:8000/instances \
  -H "X-API-Key: $ADMIN_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"role":"encode","url":"http://e-host:8001"}'

curl --fail-with-body http://proxy-host:8000/instances \
  -H "X-API-Key: $ADMIN_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"role":"prefill_decode","url":"http://pd-host:8002"}'
```

POST and DELETE operations on `/instances` require `X-API-Key`. GET can be used
to inspect the registry. Registration is idempotent, and launchers must
re-register instances after a proxy restart.

For Example and NIXL EC connectors, no additional registration fields are
needed. For Mooncake, the launcher also supplies the EC consumer's fixed
TP-rank-0 control addresses and DP size:

```json
{
  "role": "prefill_decode",
  "url": "http://pd-host:8002",
  "dp_size": 2,
  "ec_zmq_addrs": ["tcp://pd-host:19019", "tcp://pd-host:19021"]
}
```

The proxy keeps the selected consumer replica and its control address together
for the encoder push and inference request.

The `disagg_1e1pd_example.sh` and `disagg_1e1p1d_example.sh` scripts support this
mode through `DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION=1` and `ADMIN_API_KEY`; static routing remains
the default.

## Availability behavior

- Periodic health probes stop routing to an instance after the configured
  consecutive-failure threshold.
- Recovered instances rejoin automatically.
- Unreachable instances are evicted after `--evicted-ttl` unless it is `0`.
- Explicit removal stops new routing without changing already selected routes.
- Probe interval, timeout, failure threshold, and eviction TTL are configurable.

## Validation

Model evaluation (earlier revision):

```bash
CONCURRENCY=1 REPEAT=1 MAX_MODEL_LEN=16384 \
  bash tests/v1/ec_connector/integration/run_epd_mooncake_ec_full_pipeline.sh
```

Qwen2.5-VL-3B with Mooncake TCP and CUDA graphs enabled: single-image,
two-image, and repeated-image responses matched the colocated baseline (3/3).
This E2E/model evaluation has not been rerun on the current revision.

## Duplicate-work check

No other open PR found by searches for dynamic EPD registration or EPD proxy
implements launcher-managed HTTP instance registration. Related open PRs cover
documentation, proxy bug fixes, transfer lifecycle, or EC connectors rather
than this registry and routing behavior.

AI assistance was used. The submitter reviewed the changes and validation
results.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Reuse the decode topk ragged metadata across layers
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose `_forward_decode` rebuilds the ragged form of the topk indices on every compressed layer. The pack is a pure function of the shared `topk_indices_buffer`, which only `index_source_layer_ids` write, plus per-step metadata (`token_to_req_indices`, the block table, `is_valid_token`). The one per-layer term is `compress_ratio`, which divides the block size. So the layers between two index sources all rebuild the same thing. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `compress_ratios` has 38 layers with a compressed cache and `index_source_layer_ids` has 8 entries, giving 38 rebuilds per decode step for 8 distinct results — a 4.8x redundancy. A 10-step decode trace on MI355X (TP4, rank 0) confirms the count and the cost: | kernel | total | calls | per call | |---|---|---|---| | `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel` | 1678.1 us | 380 | 4.42 us | | `_compute_topk_lens_kernel` | 1546.0 us | 380 | 4.07 us | 380 = 38 layers x 10 steps. Together they are 2.2% of all kernel time, ~322 us and 76 launches per step. ## What changes The index source memoizes the pack and the layers below it read through, keyed by compress ratio since that is the only per-layer term. Consumers resolve their source once in `__init__` through `static_forward_context`, the same way the layer already resolves its compressed-KV source, and raise the same `NotImplementedError` if a PP split lands inside an index-sharing group. Invalidation is structural rather than versioned: the source clears its own entry when it runs, and it always runs before the layers that consume its indices, so a step cannot read the previous step's pack. Prefill is untouched. Expected effect: 8 rebuilds per step instead of 38, ~255 us and 60 launches per step of GPU work removed, ~1.8% of decode GPU time on this model. ## Not a duplicate Searched open PRs for the neighbouring work: - #56638 re-enables the fused `combine_topk_swa_indices` kernel. Same file, but the mixed-prefill index combine, not the decode pack. - #57282 adds an opt-in HIP decode kernel. It consumes this metadata; it does not change how often it is built. - #57109 and #54394 touch the indexer that produces the indices, upstream of the pack. None of them change the per-layer rebuild. ## Test plan - `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py` - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X: a 10-step decode capture to confirm the rebuild count drops to one per index source, and GSM8K for accuracy parity. The change is a pure memoization, so parity is the bar. ## Test results Unit tests, on the branch, MI355X: ``` $ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -q 68 passed in 75.03s ``` Decode capture, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 on MI355X, 10 engine steps at concurrency 1, fp8 KV, MTP spec decode. Per-step kernel time, mean over the four TP ranks: | kernel | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel` | 173.1 us | 38.0 us | | `_compute_topk_lens_kernel` | 158.4 us | 34.1 us | | `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` (untouched) | 201.6 us | 206.5 us | | `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` (untouched) | 218.7 us | 224.1 us | Launches fall from 380 to 80 per 10 steps, i.e. exactly the 8 per step the 8 index sources predict, and the untouched kernels stay put. Net 250.2 us per step against the 255 us the trace analysis predicted. Accuracy, GSM8K 5-shot, 400 questions, greedy, concurrency 32, spec decode off so that generations are model-faithful: | build | accuracy | invalid | |---|---|---| | main | 0.9025 | 0.0% | | this PR | 0.9025 | 0.0% | Note this stack is not run-to-run deterministic: `main` compared against itself disagrees token-for-token on 3 of 6 fixed greedy prompts, so parity is established statistically rather than by diffing outputs. ## What is not measured End-to-end interactivity, which this PR does not claim. Paired step-time samples on MI355X (TP4, MTP spec decode, profiler off, three 25 s samples per point, `main` and the patched build loaded side by side on opposite GPU halves) do not resolve a change of this size. The patched side here carries this change together with #57435: | concurrency | main | patched | delta | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 45.57 +/- 1.24 ms/step | 46.15 +/- 1.21 | +1.28% | | 32 | 44.65 +/- 0.21 ms/step | 44.41 +/- 0.08 | -0.54% | Acceptance was identical at 3.533 tokens per step, so the comparison is fair. The concurrency-32 point moves the right way and is by far the tighter of the two, but three samples cannot separate a sub-1% effect from this spread, and the concurrency-1 spread is larger than the effect being looked for. With spec decode off the loop is outright host-bound -- 12.61 +/- 0.00 ms per step, with the A/B at -0.01% and 0.00% -- so removed GPU work simply lands in host slack. The claim here is therefore the kernel-level saving above, not an ITL number. --- AI assistance was used to write this change. I have reviewed every line, ran the tests and evals above myself, and am responsible for it.

commits.pr_title: [Test][Core] Compute the expected hybrid prefix-cache hit instead of hard-coding it
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`test_prefix_cache_hit_rate` asserts hard-coded hit-rate floors of 0.90 / 0.75. As https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57127 documents, those numbers came from a GB200 run where the hybrid cache resolves to 544-token blocks, giving 3264 cached tokens for base and 2720 for MTP; the floors were set just below the measured minimums.

However, the block size is not portable. It is derived at startup from the mamba state size divided by the per-token KV size, rounded up to the attention backend's minimum kernel block — and that last term is platform-specific. On XPU the same model resolves to 576-token blocks:

| platform | min kernel block | resolved block size | best possible hit | hit rate | passes 0.90? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA | 16 | 544 | `6 * 544 = 3264` | 98.1% | ✅ |
| XPU | 64 | 576 | `5 * 576 = 2880` | 86.6% | ❌ |

Both engines return exactly the optimum. The gap is a rounding artifact, not a behavior difference: `3274 = 6*544 + 10` but `3274 = 5*576 + 394`. Changing the GPU, TP size, or KV cache dtype can flip the result either way, so the floors encode luck rather than a contract.

This PR keeps the original intent but replaces the hard-coded floors with the theoretical optimum, computed from the engine's resolved block sizes (read from `vllm:cache_config_info` ) as `round_down(previously_computed_prefix, scheduler_block_size)`. The MTP variant allows one dropped block — the EAGLE prefill-lookahead drop that #57127 measured as the 3264 → 2720 difference.

Test-only change; no runtime behavior is affected.

### Known limitations

- `vllm:cache_config_info` exposes `block_size` and `mamba_block_size`; a model with a third KV cache group would make the real `scheduler_block_size` larger than the LCM computed here. Not the case for `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`. Exposing `scheduler_block_size` through the engine handshake would remove the duplication and is left as a follow-up.

### Duplicate-work check

No open PR addresses these thresholds. This builds directly on #57127 (merged), authored by @ZJY0516. No issue is linked.

## Test Plan
```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py
```
## Test Result
- Both `base` and `mtp` variants pass on XPU and CUDA.

## AI assistance
AI assistance was used for the investigation and the patch. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests myself.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix SM100 fp8_ds_mla cache scales
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Unify the `fp8_ds_mla` cache scale contract used by FlashMLA on SM90 and
SM100. The physical 656-byte cache entry is unchanged: 512 FP8 NoPE values,
four FP32 scale fields (one per 128 values), and a 128-byte BF16 RoPE tail.
The value stored in each FP32 scale field is now always:

```text
2 ** ceil(log2(max(amax / 448, 1e-4)))
```

Power-of-two values survive both reader conversions exactly: SM90 converts
the scale to BF16, while SM100 converts it to E8M0. Arbitrary FP32 values can
therefore make the writer quantize with a different scale than the reader
uses. The `1e-4` lower bound matches the FlashMLA UE8M0 reference margin and
maps an all-zero tile to `2^-13` after rounding.

Apply the same rule to all `fp8_ds_mla` writers:

- the native CUDA cache writer;
- the fused DeepSeek-V3.2 Triton writer; and
- the Kimi K3 shared prefill/decode CUDA writer.

The tests enforce bit-compatible native, Triton, and Kimi output and exercise
the real native cache-writer-to-sparse-FlashMLA-reader path. The reader test
uses fixed-width, `-1`-padded indices so it runs with both SM90 FlashMLA V3.2
and SM100.

This is the existing PR for the cache-scale mismatch; no duplicate PR was
opened. Searches for open `fp8_ds_mla`/FlashMLA scale fixes found no competing
change. Unrelated CI regressions are tracked by their existing fixes rather
than duplicated here.

AI assistance disclosure: Codex assisted with tracing the reader/writer
contract, implementation, tests, CI diagnosis, and validation. The human
submitter must review every changed line and defend the change end-to-end.

## Validation

On NVIDIA GB300 / SM103 with CUDA 13.1:

- A full release build and install passed, including both changed CUDA
  translation units.

commits.pr_title: [GLM5.3 Perf] Size the GLM-5 sparse indexer decode workspace, 3072 MiB GPU memory saved
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

1. Rename `max_model_len` to `max_pool_len` for GLM indexer

2. Size the GLM-5 sparse indexer decode workspace using the pooled sequence length:

`max_pool_len = max_model_len // index_kpool`

This reduces the decode logits workspace without changing model behavior

By default model len `1,048,576` we get 4x memory reduction, namely 3072 MiB memory saved

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

A sweep through different model len

```py
"""
import statistics

import torch

from vllm.platforms import current_platform
from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import (
    fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits,
    get_num_sms,
    get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata,
)
from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_deep_gemm

TOKEN_LENGTHS = (16_384, 65_536, 262_144, 1_048_576)
KPOOL = 4
BATCH = 4
HEADS = 32
HEAD_DIM = 128
BLOCK_SIZE = 64
WARMUP = 5
REPEATS = 50

# Realistic B300 server configuration. These values match vLLM's defaults on
# GPUs with at least 160 GiB of memory.
MAX_NUM_SEQS = 1024
MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS = 16_384
NUM_SPECULATIVE_TOKENS = 0
PREFILL_WORKSPACE_MIB = 512


def benchmark(run, width):
    for _ in range(WARMUP):
        run(width)
        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

    samples = []
    start = torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end = torch.Event(enable_timing=True)
    for _ in range(REPEATS):
        start.record()
        run(width)
        end.record()
        end.synchronize()
        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end))
    return statistics.median(samples)


def profiled_workspace_mib(width):
    decode_rows = min(
        MAX_NUM_SEQS * (NUM_SPECULATIVE_TOKENS + 1), MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS
    )
    decode_mib = decode_rows * width * torch.float32.itemsize / 2**20
    return max(decode_mib, PREFILL_WORKSPACE_MIB)


@torch.inference_mode()
def run_case(token_length):
    pool_length = token_length // KPOOL
    num_blocks = pool_length // BLOCK_SIZE
    q = torch.zeros(BATCH, 1, HEADS, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
    weights = torch.ones(BATCH, HEADS, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
    kv_cache = torch.zeros(
        num_blocks,
        BLOCK_SIZE,
        1,
        HEAD_DIM + 4,
        dtype=torch.uint8,
        device="cuda",
    )
    context_lens = torch.full((BATCH, 1), pool_length, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    block_tables = (
        torch.arange(num_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        .expand(BATCH, -1)
        .contiguous()
    )
    schedule = get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(context_lens, BLOCK_SIZE, get_num_sms())

    def run(width):
        return fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits(
            (q, None),
            kv_cache,
            weights,
            context_lens,
            block_tables,
            schedule,
            width,
            clean_logits=False,
        )

    before = run(token_length)
    after = run(pool_length)
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
    torch.testing.assert_close(before[:, :pool_length], after, rtol=0, atol=0)

    before_ms = benchmark(run, token_length)
    after_ms = benchmark(run, pool_length)
    return before.nbytes / 2**20, after.nbytes / 2**20, before_ms, after_ms


def main():
    if not torch.accelerator.is_available() or not has_deep_gemm():
        raise RuntimeError("This benchmark requires CUDA and DeepGEMM")

    print(f"GPU: {current_platform.get_device_name()}")
    print(f"batch={BATCH}, index_kpool={KPOOL}, repeats={REPEATS}")
    print(
        "server: "
        f"max_num_seqs={MAX_NUM_SEQS}, "
        f"max_num_batched_tokens={MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS}, "
        f"num_speculative_tokens={NUM_SPECULATIVE_TOKENS}, "
        f"prefill_workspace={PREFILL_WORKSPACE_MIB} MiB"
    )
    print(
        "tokens     output MiB          latency ms       speedup  "
        "profiled workspace MiB"
    )
    print(
        "            before   after     before   after             "
        "before   after   saved"
    )
    for token_length in TOKEN_LENGTHS:
        before_mib, after_mib, before_ms, after_ms = run_case(token_length)
        workspace_before = profiled_workspace_mib(token_length)
        workspace_after = profiled_workspace_mib(token_length // KPOOL)
        print(
            f"{token_length:>9,}  {before_mib:>8.2f} {after_mib:>7.2f}  "
            f"{before_ms:>8.3f} {after_ms:>7.3f}  "
            f"{before_ms / after_ms:>6.3f}x  "
            f"{workspace_before:>8.0f} {workspace_after:>7.0f} "
            f"{workspace_before - workspace_after:>7.0f}"
        )
        torch.accelerator.empty_cache()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

```bash
tokens     output MiB          latency ms       speedup  profiled workspace MiB
            before   after     before   after             before   after   saved
   16,384      0.25    0.06     0.016   0.016   1.019x       512     512       0
   65,536      1.00    0.25     0.016   0.016   1.040x       512     512       0
  262,144      4.00    1.00     0.018   0.018   1.009x      1024     512     512
1,048,576     16.00    4.00     0.024   0.024   1.003x      4096    1024    3072
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Take padded path for ragged decode batches in sparse_attn_indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a crash in `sparse_attn_indexer` for ragged decode batches.

`decode_metadata.requires_padding` can be computed `False` for ragged mixed/warmup decode batches (observed on SM120/GB10 TP=2: 8 decode tokens over 6 requests). The non-padded path then performs a uniform `num_decode_tokens // batch` reshape, which crashes when the token count does not divide evenly over the decode batch.

Fix: also take the padded path whenever `num_decode_tokens % decode_lens.shape[0] != 0`. This is a strictly-safer superset of the current condition; evenly-divisible batches keep the fast path.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this condition in `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`; #47808 (DSpark confidence-scheduled verification) restructured other parts of this file but kept the `requires_padding`-only condition. The metadata-side computation (`requires_padding = min_decode_len != max_decode_len` in `backends/mla/indexer.py`) is unchanged on `main`, so the ragged case is still reachable.

## Test Plan

- `python -m py_compile vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`
- End-to-end: 2× DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), TP=2, serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731; warmup + mixed decode batches that previously produced the ragged 8-tokens-over-6-requests shape.

## Test Result

- Before: reshape crash during warmup/mixed decode batches on SM120 TP=2.
- After: serving stable on 2× DGX Spark GB10 TP=2 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731); padded path takes over for ragged batches, no perf change for uniform batches.

---

AI assistance was used for this PR (rebasing the fix from a v0.26.0-based production branch onto `main`); every changed line was reviewed and validated end-to-end by the submitter on the hardware above.

commits.pr_title: [Model Runner V2] Support custom logits processors
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add support for custom logits processors to Model Runner V2, mirroring the V1 feature with V2's batch model (#47172).

- a new `LogitsProcessor` ABC under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logits_processor/` with a single `add_request()` lifecycle keyed by the persistent slot index — no BatchUpdate ledger and no removal hook (V2 slots are never moved and freed slots are never indexed, so add-side overwrite is sufficient)
- `LogitsProcRequestState`, a narrow frozen struct passed to `__init__` that exposes only the fields a processor may read (token history, device, max_num_reqs, vocab_size), so `RequestState` stays out of the interface
- `LogitsContext`, the per-step batch layout passed to `apply()` — V2 reorders and expands logits rows every step, so a row is not a request
- a V2-own loader that validates entrypoint plugins and FQCNs against the V2 interface at load time, rejecting V1-interface processors with a clear error instead of crashing mid-sampling
- adoption of the interface by the built-in sampler states (logit bias, penalties, bad words): `add_request() -> bool` is OR-ed into `needs_logits_processing`, and `apply_staged_writes()` is the optional per-step flush hook for host-staged writes
- removes "custom logits processors" from the V2-unsupported gate: they no longer force a silent fallback to the V1 runner (or a hard error when V2 is forced)
- ports V1's `validate_params` to the V2 interface as an optional classmethod, dispatched at request admission by the active model runner: V1 keeps the existing path byte for byte, V2 runs the new entry

No behavior change for the pre-existing sampling stages; their pipeline order is unchanged. Custom processors run after the built-in stages and before thinking-budget forcing and temperature.

Documents the MRV2 logits processor interface in `docs/features/custom_logitsprocs.md`.

## Duplicate work check

#47585 adapts the V1 interface via a bridge: it diffs the row→request assignment every step to synthesize V1 `BatchUpdate` events, and mirrors output tokens on CPU from the AsyncOutput D2H copy. That doesn't fit MRV2:

1. **MRV2 has no BatchUpdate.** V1 needs the added/removed/moved ledger only because its batch indices compact and move; MRV2 slots are persistent and never moved. The bridge re-derives via per-step diffs what the runner already knows — a synthetic event stream instead of real lifecycle calls.
2. **The persistent batch model differs.** MRV2 reorders logits rows every step and expands them under speculative decoding (a row is not a request). The bridge assumes V1's row==request semantics, pays a per-step CPU diff + D2H sync to reconstruct state MRV2 already keeps on-device, and cannot represent draft rows — so it inherits V1's "no custom processors under spec decode" restriction, which MRV2-native processors don't have.
3. The bridge keeps V1's runtime costs (per-step diffing, CPU token mirrors, argmax-invariance routing) instead of exploiting MRV2's strengths (stable slots, on-device token history, admission gating via `add_request()`'s return).

This PR therefore implements a V2-native interface and rejects V1-interface processors at load time with a clear error, rather than wrapping them.

## Test Plan

- New CPU-only loader tests (`tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py`): V1-interface rejection via class object / FQCN / entrypoint, non-type and unimportable FQCNs, pooling-model rejection, load order, `validate_params` admission behavior.
- New GPU integration test (`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py`): a recording custom processor driven through `Sampler` — hook order, logits modification, pipeline position (post-bias, pre-temperature).
- New regressions: custom processor's `add_request()` return gating `needs_logits_processing`; slot reuse clearing bad-words state; custom LPs absent from the V2-unsupported gate (`tests/test_config.py`); `verify()` stays runner-agnostic (`tests/test_sampling_params.py`).
- Adapted existing suites: logit bias, bad words, sampler flags, thinking budget.
- E2E on NVIDIA GB200 with Qwen/Qwen3-8B: `vllm serve` with a target-token custom processor (correctness: forced output matches the target token exactly; untouched requests unaffected), `vllm bench serve` baseline vs loaded-processor throughput, and startup rejection of a V1-interface processor.

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logit_bias.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_bad_words.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py \
    tests/test_config.py::test_v2_model_runner_supports_custom_logits_processors \
    tests/test_sampling_params.py::test_verify_leaves_logits_processors_to_admission -v
```

## Test Result

- Units: 50 passed on NVIDIA GB200.
- E2E (Qwen3-8B, MRV2): serve with the custom processor starts under the V2 runner with no fallback; forced requests emit exactly the target token, plain requests unaffected; a V1-interface processor is rejected at engine init with a clear error.

Bench on GB200 (`vllm bench serve`, random 128/128, 256 prompts, concurrency 32, warmup + median of 7 runs). The processor is loaded but no request activates it:

| Config | Output token/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Delta v. baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 7,081 | 71.5 | 3.98 | 0.0% |
| Custom LP loaded | 7,074 | 71.7 | 3.98 | -0.1% (within run-to-run noise) |
